name: Frequent Subgraphs in One Labeled Graph
problem_statement: Enumerate or count connected labeled patterns meeting a declared minimum-image-support threshold in one labeled host graph.

normalization: Preserve external vertex identities and isolated vertices.
Reject self-loops and collapse parallel edges only under the declared aggregation rule.

problem_inputs.name: minimum_image_support
problem_inputs.description: Positive minimum over pattern vertices of the number of distinct host images.

problem_inputs.name: max_pattern_edges
problem_inputs.description: Positive maximum number of pattern edges.

problem_inputs.name: output_mode
problem_inputs.description: Pattern records or a count of distinct frequent isomorphism classes.

required_outputs.name: frequent_pattern_count
required_outputs.description: Number of distinct frequent labeled connected pattern isomorphism classes.

required_outputs.name: patterns
required_outputs.description: Canonical labeled patterns and MNI support when output_mode=patterns; null in count mode.

required_outputs.name: completed
required_outputs.description: Whether enumeration completed through the requested size bound.

solution_semantics.objective: Enumerate or count connected labeled patterns meeting a declared minimum-image-support threshold in one labeled host graph.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mathematical objective; implementations must declare approximation and termination status.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Each external vertex ID occurs once; output multiplicities follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No ordering among equally valid solutions is required.

validation_rules: For each pattern vertex independently collect distinct host images; support is the smallest image-set size.
Use exhaustive embeddings on tiny labeled graphs as a correctness oracle.
Do not substitute transaction support, number of embeddings, or edge-disjoint support for MNI.
Count-only upstream releases cannot satisfy the patterns output mode without an adapter change.
edge_cases: Repeated labels do not identify distinct host vertices.
A single host graph differs from a database of graph transactions.
A threshold exceeding the host vertex count yields no frequent patterns.
